title: Section 3(p) - Indian Patents Act, 1970
official_citation: The Patents Act, 1970 (Act No. 39 of 1970), Section 3(p)
summary: An invention which in effect, is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components is not patentable.
key_clauses: Traditional formulations described in authoritative Ayurvedic treatises (e.g. Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Sahasrayogam) are barred from patentability as prior art.

Novel delivery mechanisms (liposomes, nanoparticles, specialized controlled-release matrices) of Ayurvedic extracts can overcome Section 3(p) if substantial synergy or technological leap is demonstrated.
Novel standardized extraction processes yielding unprecedented therapeutic biomarker profiles with inventive steps may be patentable as process patents.
practical_guidance: Applicants must demonstrate synergy (non-obvious combination) exceeding mere additive effect under Section 3(e) and non-obvious efficacy improvements under Section 3(d) with quantitative pharmacological data.

title: Section 3(d) & Section 3(e) - Efficacy and Admixture Bar
official_citation: The Patents Act, 1970, Section 3(d) and Section 3(e)
summary: Section 3(d) prevents evergreening by excluding mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy. Section 3(e) bars a substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in aggregation of properties.
key_clauses: For Ayurvedic polyherbal mixtures, merely mixing known herbs (e.g., Turmeric + Neem + Tulsi) is rejected under Section 3(e) as a mere admixture unless synergistic bio-enhancement is statistically proven.
Enhanced therapeutic efficacy under 3(d) must be demonstrated in clinical or robust in-vivo models, not merely chemical yield or bioavailability changes without therapeutic impact.
practical_guidance: Provide Compounding Index (CI) or isobologram analysis demonstrating synergy (CI < 1.0) to successfully counter Section 3(e) objections in the First Examination Report (FER).
